newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Deal signed to promote electronic commerce in China.
newsitem.headline: Deal signed to promote electronic commerce in China.

text.p: A cooperation agreement has been signed between CargoNet, a Hong Kong based electronic service provider and the Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC) to promote electronic commerce services for Hong Kong companies doing business in China.

A CargoNet statement said the agreement will also provide software testing services to help corporate and third-party software developers integrate their products and systems with CargoNet's network-based electronic commerce solutions.

The HKPC "is the territory's premier technology transfer agency supporting local enterprises. It also has a well established role supporting cross-border businesses that operate both in Hong Kong and China. It is therefore a very strong partner in the promotion of CargoNet's vision of full electronic commerce within Hong Kong and its economic hinterland," said Ian Craig, Chief Executive of CargoNet.

Dr James Fok, HKPC's Branch Director for Design and Information Technology "We have been working on electronic commerce solutions to support Hong Kong business since 1989. Earlier this year, we were given a specific mandate by the government's Trade and Industry Branch to step up our activities in this area.
